localNote.q: How do you book a Michelin star restaurant in Chicago?
localNote.a: Mostly on Tock, which was started in Chicago by {r:alinea}’s co-owner Nick Kokonas. Alinea, {r:oriole}, {r:next} and many of the city’s other tasting menus sell their tables there as prepaid tickets: you pay for the meal when you book, refunds are rare, and you can usually pass the booking to a friend instead. Most of the rest are on OpenTable, among them {r:boka}, {r:topolobampo} and {r:sepia}, and a few on Resy.

localNote.q: When do tables open at Chicago’s starred restaurants?
localNote.a: Further ahead than in most US cities. Alinea releases each month’s tables on the 15th, two months before, at 11am Central time. Oriole books 90 days ahead, {r:esme} and Sepia about two months, and {r:kasama} six weeks ahead at noon.

localNote.q: What should you wear to a Michelin star restaurant in Chicago?
localNote.a: Chicago is relaxed. {r:ever}, Oriole, Esmé and {r:elske} say they have no dress code at all, and Alinea asks only for “elevated casual”. Smart casual fits everywhere.

localNote.q: How much should you tip in Chicago?
localNote.a: Check the bill first. Many of the city’s starred restaurants add a service charge to pay their whole team: 20% at Alinea, Ever and {r:indienne}, 22% at Esmé. Where there’s one, anything more is up to you; where there isn’t, tip 18–22% of the bill before tax.
